primary_variables.matched_definition: Chemical treatment that perturbs protein folding, degradation, chaperone function, or proteome stability.
evidence: The main goal of this study was to analyze the degradome of HF3 in human plasma.
In order to assess the proteolytic activity of HF3 on a wide spectrum of proteins, we used untargeted peptidomics to detect the degradation products by mass spectrometry.

attributes.dose_or_concentration: 0.5 μg (for P(Alb-D), P(20-MAP-D), P(LAP-E)) and 2 μg (for P(W))
attributes.route_or_context: incubated in 250 mM ammonium acetate containing CaCl2 1 mM at 37 °C
evidence: P(Alb-D), P(20-MAP-D), and P(LAP-E); 50 μg were separately incubated with 0.5 μg HF3 (1:100; w/w) in 250 mM ammonium acetate containing CaCl2 1 mM for 2 h at 37 °C.
P(W) (200 μg) was incubated with 2 μg HF3 under the same conditions.

control_arms: Samples of P(Alb-D), P(20-MAP-D), P(LAP-E), and P(W) were incubated without HF3
replicate_hints: Three individual experiments of incubation of plasma proteins with HF3 were carried out with each of the four types of plasma samples
For each of the four types of human plasma preparations, three biological replicates were performed.

evidence: peptides identified in the control samples were disregarded in the analysis, therefore only proteins that showed peptides identified exclusively in the sample of plasma treated with HF3 were considered

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data was acquired in data-dependent mode (DDA) using an LTQ-Orbitrap Velos. While 'peptide counting' is mentioned in PRIDE metadata, the untargeted peptidomics approach for identifying cleavage products typically maps to a label-free quantification (LFQ) or spectral counting base.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment is explicitly described as 'untargeted peptidomics' to explore the 'pathodegradome'. Search parameters explicitly state 'no enzyme specificity indicated' because the peptides are products of HF3 proteolytic activity, not tryptic digestion.
